title: Template: SaaS Board Growth Diagnostics Bundle
goal: Generate a board-ready SaaS operating review bundle from frozen multi-table revenue, product, marketing, and support data; validate the metrics through a live localhost audit API; and submit a final report package that remains internally consistent.
skillBenefitRationale: The bound skill standardizes the highest-cost parts of the workflow: contract probing, metric diffing against the live validator, diagnosis scaffolding, and final bundle packaging against the localhost audit chain. Without the skill the task remains theoretically solvable from the visible data and contract, but the solver has to recover the diagnosis path and final submission closure manually at much higher time/token cost.
designGoals: Keep the task centered on a realistic board-level data analysis deliverable rather than a code-fix exercise.
Preserve a real localhost audit chain inside one container instead of reducing validation to static golden files.
Require multi-table data integration and cross-artifact consistency across CSV, JSON, Markdown, and final submission payloads.
Let verifier focus on behavioral correctness and live-chain acceptance rather than one exact implementation path.

mainTests: The required CSV, JSON, Markdown, submission bundle, and audit receipt all exist and are parseable.
metrics_snapshot.csv matches the published metric contract when recomputed from the frozen raw data.
diagnosis_report.json and executive_summary.md surface the true growth, risk, efficiency, and support-product signals present in the data.
The final submission remains consistent with the standalone files and is accepted by the live audit API.
guardrails: Protected raw data and hidden audit service entrypoint remain unchanged.
The solver must use the live manifest -> validate-metrics -> submit-report chain and keep the final saved bundle aligned with the submitted payload.
Static placeholder outputs, empty findings, or hardcoded receipts do not pass.

notes: with_skill and without_skill experiment copies used the same task content, data, tests, verifier, and dependencies.
The without-skill runs only stripped environment/skills and the corresponding Docker COPY-skills lines in the temporary runtime copy used for that comparison.
The final hidden service no longer exposes a directly readable on-disk private implementation blob during normal solving, while verifier restartability remains stable.
